figures.pedagogical_necessity: The recurrence's one stored value is easy to compute but hard to see as an infinite impulse response. A four-frame sequence makes one extra loop traversal and one extra delayed term perceptible without duplicating the later state ledger.
figures.tier_reason: The repeated loop, four short symbolic gain labels, and fixed term slots form a small geometric process. Raw SVG preserves pixel-identical frames and avoids forcing a hook-free React sequence around simple arrows and boxes.
figures.source_status: house drawing inspired by MIT 6.003 Session 2 slides 36-56; recreate the idea, do not trace the slides
figures.embed: <FigureSequence name="feedback-tail-unroll" alt="Four frames unroll the first-order feedback rule y[n]=a y[n-1]+x[n] into delayed feedforward terms with gains 1, a, a squared, and a cubed while showing the old state read before each write." caption="Each traversal of the delay-and-gain loop adds one sample of the infinite tail h[n]=a^n u[n]." />
figures.teaching_claim: One delay-and-gain state update is equivalent, from initial rest, to successively exposing feedforward terms x[n], ax[n-1], a^2x[n-2], and onward.

fixed_elements: top recurrence y[n]=x[n]+a y[n-1] with sum, gain a, unit delay, and explicit READ old state before WRITE new state
bottom four-slot unrolled path ledger for delays 0 through 3
ellipsis/tail continuation after the fourth slot
shared_layout.frame_delta: Frames 1 through 4 activate exactly the next loop traversal and corresponding slot: 1, a, a^2, then a^3. Previously revealed slots remain fixed; all geometry, axes, arrows, and labels are pixel-identical.

acceptance: The feedback arrow visibly reads the old state before the write arrow updates it.
The four frames expose 1,a,a^2,a^3 in order and do not imply a finite tail.

Light and dark renders retain all arrows, ghost slots, superscripts, and color-redundant labels.

figures.pedagogical_necessity: This is the lesson's literal implementation check. The prose gives coefficients and outputs, but only the ledger exposes which two old values are read and how the newly computed output shifts into state.
figures.tier_reason: Five rows carry formulas, signed decimal arithmetic, and responsive state pairs. HTML grid plus shared KaTeX is safer and more legible than hand-positioned SVG text, especially on mobile.
figures.source_status: house component using the lesson/demo's reconciled recurrence; no sourced artifact
figures.embed: <Figure name="ResonatorStateLedger" alt="A five-row ledger steps an initially resting second-order resonator through a unit impulse, showing each old state pair, computed output, and shifted new state pair." caption="Each sample reads both old outputs before shifting the newly computed output into state." />
figures.teaching_claim: The verified impulse samples arise only when both old outputs are read before either stored value is overwritten.
figures.composition: Top strip binds f_s=1000 Hz, f_0=180 Hz, r=0.970, a1=0.8260118, and a2=-0.9409 to the recurrence. Below, five responsive row cards preserve the left-to-right order n/x -> old pair -> arithmetic y[n] -> new pair. Use auto-fit cards so a 360 px view stacks without reducing formula text below legibility.

figures.pedagogical_necessity: The root formulas are abstract until pole geometry and sample behavior are synchronized. The three controlled cases separate a real decay from conjugate oscillation and then change only conjugate radius to cross the stability boundary.
figures.tier_reason: This is a three-way comparison with formula labels, repeated semantic bindings, and a mobile stacking requirement. A responsive HTML card grid with small inline SVG pole planes/stem plots and KaTeX labels follows the component-figure contract.
figures.source_status: house component inspired by MIT 6.003 Session 3 and Lyons Chapter 6; recreate the concept, not source artwork
figures.embed: <Figure name="PoleModePairings" alt="Three paired pole plots and discrete modes show a real pole at 0.70 decaying, conjugate poles of radius 0.97 producing a damped oscillation, and conjugate poles of radius 1.02 producing a growing oscillation at the same angle." caption="Pole angle fixes oscillation rate; pole radius decides whether the mode decays or grows." />
figures.teaching_claim: Holding angle at 0.36 pi while moving conjugate radius from 0.97 to 1.02 preserves oscillation rate and reverses the envelope from decay to growth.
figures.composition: Three numbered cards use identical pole-plane and n=0..12 stem-plot geometry with one common y scale [-1.3,1.3]. Card 1 has one real pole and n=0..9; Cards 2 and 3 use the same +/-0.36 pi angle and differ only in radius. On mobile the cards stack; within each card pole plane sits above the stem plot.

All series begin at 1; label the three n=99 endpoints directly. A rightward continuation arrow names the three infinite-tail outcomes, and a bottom verdict separates finite boundedness from absolute summability.

global_visual_rules.reading_order: left-to-right for one state update and top-to-bottom when responsive cards stack
global_visual_rules.palette: currentColor plus amber #e2903a, blue #4c8dd6, and green #5aa46a only
global_visual_rules.theme_contract: Raw SVG text/strokes use currentColor and opacity for secondary roles; components use palette.ts and site ink/muted values. No baked white background or fixed black text.
global_visual_rules.accessibility: Color is redundant with READ/WRITE labels, pole position, stem/dot shape, card titles, endpoint values, and decay/grow/summable text.
global_visual_rules.math_notation: Use n for sample index, j for the imaginary unit, omega0 in radians/sample, f0 in cycles/sample or Hz only with f_s, rho for radius, and the implementation signs a1=+2rho cos(omega0), a2=-rho^2.
global_visual_rules.discrete_plot_rule: Use stems or individual dots for sampled sequences; do not connect samples with curves that imply between-sample behavior.
global_visual_rules.sourcing: All four visuals explain course-owned calculations or constructions. None is an authenticity-bearing artifact, photograph, scan, or measured data plot, so sourced count is zero.
